location: filters, search, legend counts, list, address
what_is_wrong: Checked: topic, records found, kind, status, country, organisation, "Only sites on the map" and the search each change the markers, the counts beside the legend, the list and the address; reloading the address brings the same view back.
evidence: Desktop and phone, light and dark. ?topic=5&holds=rec: 14 of 989 sites, 11 on the map, legend 11/0/0, 11 markers. ?country=GBR: 73 sites, 47 markers, all inside the map after it refits. ?status=permitted: 195 sites, 129 markers. Reloading ?topic=5&holds=rec&kind=datacenter&status=operating&country=IRL and ?q=google gave back the same selects, counts (11 of 989 · 9 on the map; 37 of 989 · 35 on the map), legend and list. A search with no match shows "No site matches..." and zero counts. Clear empties the address. No script errors.

location: topic: marker colours and legend wording
what_is_wrong: Checked: choosing a topic recolours the markers by what is found on that topic and rewrites the legend.
evidence: Every topic: 471 green, 6 orange, 153 hollow markers. Water: 11 green, 619 hollow. Electricity used: 206 green, 424 hollow. The legend reads "at least one figure from a record on water / only claims on water / no figure on water yet", and the list column becomes "Records found (Water) 3 from records". Screenshot map_desktop_light_topic_electricity.png.

what_is_wrong: Checked: map.html?site=<id> opens that site, and its popup lists the figures topic by topic, with links.
evidence: ?site=irl-amazon-airton-road-tallaght-dub56-p1173 opens the popup in view: "Electricity used: 3 from records / Greenhouse gases: 4 computed / Generators, fuel and air pollution: 6 from records · 2 computed / Water: 3 from records / 1 chain link / Open the site page · All its figures". Each topic links to explore.html?subject=...&topic=N, and every link responds. The Electricity link lands on Explore showing 3 figures under a banner. Screenshot map_desktop_light_site_popup.png.

what_is_wrong: Checked: the banner and the group's sites, and "Show every site".
evidence: The banner reads "Showing the sites of Amazon.com, Inc. and of the companies a document says belong to its group (its page). Show every site". The page shows 75 of 989 sites with 56 markers; all 75 rows are in the group's list (75 expected). "Show every site" returns to 989 and empties the address. Every organisation page with a placed site links to map.html?org=<its id> (190 links, all valid). Screenshot map_desktop_light_org_amazon.png.

what_is_wrong: Checked: every control can be reached by Tab and used from the keyboard, and focus is visible.
evidence: Tab order: search box, topic, records found, kind, status, country, organisation, checkbox, Clear, the map, list links, Show on map, Show more. An arrow key on Topic changed the map and the address (?topic=0). Typing in the search filtered the sites. Space ticked the checkbox and Enter worked Clear. Enter or Space on a focused marker opens its popup, and its tooltip shows the name. Focus is a 2px accent outline on fields and buttons, with a ring on the map, in light and dark. Screenshot map_focus_rings_combined.png.

what_is_wrong: Checked: nothing overflows the page width at 390 px, and the controls are usable.
evidence: scrollWidth 390 = clientWidth 390 in light and dark, at first load, with a popup open and with the organisation banner. Filters are full width (358 px) and 34 px high, and the Clear and Download buttons are 33 px high. Screenshots map_phone_light_initial.png and map_phone_dark_org_topic.png.

what_is_wrong: The Status select picks up the style written for the page's status/loading message (#status{font-family:mono;font-size:13px;margin:14px 0}). It shows in a smaller monospace type than the other filters and has 14 px margins above and below, so the filter rows are spaced unevenly.
evidence: Computed style of the Status select: monospace, 13px, margin 14px 0. Kind select: serif, 15px, margin 0. The difference is visible in map_desktop_light_initial.png and map_phone_dark_org_topic.png ("Any status" in a different type, with extra space around it).
suggested_fix: Give the select another id (and update KEYS), or narrow the rule to the loading paragraph (e.g. p#status,#loading).

what_is_wrong: At 390 px the popup is wider than the map. Its right edge is cut off, including the close button and the ends of lines ("Tallaght (Airton Road / Belgard Road, Dubli").
evidence: Popup box spans x=69 to 400. The map ends at x=374 and the viewport is 390. Same in light and dark. Screenshots map_phone_dark_popup.png and map_phone_light_popup.png.
suggested_fix: On narrow screens, cap the popup's maxWidth at the map width less the pan padding (e.g. min(300, map width - 80)), or reduce the left pan padding (52 px) so the popup can be panned fully into view.

location: list of sites below the map, phone width
what_is_wrong: At 390 px the list table is squeezed into four columns. The Site and Kind columns are about 40 px wide, so names break letter by letter ("Ama / zon / Data / Servi / ces,") and each row is about 240 px tall. The list is hard to read on a phone.
evidence: Measured on ?org=co-amazon: column widths 42 / 40 / (Where hidden) / 168 / 108 px, row height 240 px. Screenshot map_phone_light_list.png.
suggested_fix: Below 760 px, show each row as a card (as explore.html does for its table): name and operator on one line, kind and status, then what the ledger holds and the Show on map button.

location: keyboard: markers in the Tab order
what_is_wrong: Every marker is a Tab stop between the map and the list. At the default view a keyboard user must press Tab 630 times to get past the map to the legend, the download button and the list.
evidence: Tabbing from the map container went through 630 markers before reaching the next control. The markers have no accessible name (only a tooltip).
suggested_fix: Add a "Skip the map, go to the list" link before the map, or take markers out of the Tab order (every placed site already has a "Show on map" button in the list) and give the map one Tab stop.

what_is_wrong: After "Show on map" is pressed from the keyboard, the popup opens and the page scrolls to the map, but focus stays on the button, which is now off screen. The popup's links are far back in the Tab order.
evidence: From the 30th row, it took 59 presses of Shift+Tab to reach the popup's close button. Focus after the press: the "Show on map" button (not in view).
suggested_fix: After opening the popup, move focus into it (its first link or the close button), and send focus back to the button when the popup closes.

what_is_wrong: Pressing "Show every site" removes the banner link, and focus falls back to the start of the page.
evidence: document.activeElement after Enter on #unorg: BODY (by mouse and by keyboard).
suggested_fix: After clearing the organisation, move focus to the Organisation select or to the count.

what_is_wrong: Escape does not close a popup while focus is inside it.
evidence: With focus on the popup's close button, Escape left the popup open.
suggested_fix: Close the popup on Escape from inside it and return focus to whatever opened it.

location: popup and map credit links; zoom buttons in dark
what_is_wrong: Links in the popup and in the map credit line use the map component's default blue (#0078A8), not the site's link colour. In the dark scheme this blue is about 3.6:1 against the popup background (#121816), below 4.5:1 for small text. The zoom buttons stay white in the dark scheme.
evidence: Computed link colour rgb(0,120,168) in light and dark. Popup background rgb(18,24,22) in dark. Screenshots map_desktop_dark_popup.png and map_desktop_dark_mapview.png.
suggested_fix: Set the colour of links inside the map to var(--accent), and give the zoom buttons the dark paper and ink colours in the dark scheme.

location: list column "What the ledger holds" with a topic chosen
what_is_wrong: For a site with nothing on the chosen topic, the cell says the same thing twice: "No figures yet (Water)" and then "No figures on this topic yet".
evidence: ?topic=5: first row reads "No figures yet (Water) No figures on this topic yet".
suggested_fix: Write it once, e.g. "No figures on water yet", and keep the second line for counts only.

location: site names in the list, tooltips and popups
what_is_wrong: Some site names are placeholders or raw register text. Two Chicago sites are called "not found". The list opens with "? Network Operations Center" and "^VADATA, Inc. IAD-14/52/59". 39 sites are all called "Amazon Data Services, Inc.", so on ?org=co-amazon only the county tells them apart.
evidence: Site ids usa-bench-chicago-1432-s-clinton-st and usa-bench-chicago-601-w-polk-st are named "not found" and placed on the map. The first two rows of the unfiltered list are "? Network Operations Center" and "^VADATA...". Screenshot map_desktop_dark_list.png.
suggested_fix: Where a record gives no usable name, build one from the address or permit number (e.g. "1432 S Clinton St, Chicago"). Remove the stray leading "?" and "^". Add the permit number or street to the repeated Amazon names.

what_is_wrong: map.html?site=<id> with an id that does not exist shows the full map and says nothing.
evidence: ?site=does-not-exist: no popup, no banner, 989 of 989 sites.
suggested_fix: Say so in the banner, as Explore does for an unknown figure id ("No site has the id ...").

location: filters that leave nothing on the map
what_is_wrong: With a choice whose sites have no coordinates, e.g. Kind = Smelter or refiner (75 sites, 0 on the map), the map stays at its previous view and is empty, with nothing on the map to explain why.
evidence: ?kind=smelter_refiner: "75 of 989 sites · 0 on the map", legend 0/0/0, no markers. Screenshot map_desktop_light_only_kind.png.
suggested_fix: Show a short note over the empty map: "None of these 75 sites is placed yet; they are listed below."

what_is_wrong: Only the Status options show counts ("Operating (62)"), and those counts are for all sites, not the current selection. Topic, kind and country show none.
evidence: Status options: Operating (62), A permit issued (195) ... Not stated (682), unchanged under other filters.
suggested_fix: Either show counts on every filter and update them with the selection, as Explore does, or drop them from Status.

location: "Show on map" buttons on a phone
what_is_wrong: The "Show on map" buttons are 24 px tall, small to tap on a phone.
evidence: Button box 97 x 24 px at 390 px width.
suggested_fix: Make them at least 32 to 44 px tall on narrow screens.

what_is_wrong: Checked: the country and topic filters, the search, the count and the empty state.
evidence: "47 of 47 shown" at first. Ireland: 17. Ireland + Water: 4. Search "seattle": 11. "Stella Towers": 3. United States + Water and search "zzzz" both give "0 of 47 shown" and "Nothing matches these filters.". Clearing restores 47. Screenshot totals_desktop_light_empty.png.

what_is_wrong: Checked: each row's list opens and closes.
evidence: Clicking the summary opens and then closes the list. Enter opens it and Space closes it. The summary shows a focus ring. Screenshot totals_desktop_light_row_open.png.

location: cards on a phone; long names; sums
what_is_wrong: Checked: rows become cards on a phone, long names wrap, and the sums are readable and correct.
evidence: At 390 px the header row is hidden. Each cell is a block labelled Where / What is added / Sum / What it covers. No page overflow in light or dark, even with lists open. Long names such as "Amazon Clonshaugh Business & Technology Park data storage campus (Buildings W, X, Y; U and V under licence review)" wrap. Sums are 19px bold with TWh/GWh beneath. Each of the 47 sums, recomputed from the figures its list shows, matches; every total has one figure per site, one period and one definition, all records. Screenshot totals_phone_light_cards.png.

location: emission totals t36 to t47, opened list, phone width
what_is_wrong: At 390 px the values in the opened list do not wrap. "0.0022800000 short tons = 0.00207 tonnes · the figure" runs past the right edge of the list, cutting off the "the figure" link ("· the"), so each line has to be scrolled sideways inside the list.
evidence: Values running past the edge: t36 94, t37 53, t38 94, t39 53, t40 90, t41 50, t42 90, t43 50, t44 59, t45 40, t46 91, t47 51. t44 list scrollWidth 423 against clientWidth 358. Screenshot totals_phone_light_t44_open.png.
suggested_fix: On narrow screens let .tot details li .v wrap (white-space:normal), or put "the figure" on its own line.

location: row summary "N figures added · M left out"
what_is_wrong: The summary counts figures of another definition, which have their own total, as "left out". Nothing was left out of the biomass total in t5, yet it says "11 figures added · 10 left out"; the 10 are diesel figures, with their own total in t6. A reader takes "left out" to mean excluded from this sum.
evidence: t5 "11 figures added · 10 left out", whose list holds only "The same kind of figure with another definition, not added to this one: light fuel oil (diesel) ... 10 figures · its own total". The same pattern appears in t6 to t12, t18, t19, t21 to t23, t25 to t28, t30 and t31 (t19: "12 figures added · 97 left out").
suggested_fix: Count them apart, e.g. "11 figures added · 10 of another definition (their own total)", and keep "left out" for figures excluded by a rule (approximate value, two figures for one site).

location: "none left out" against the Explore link
what_is_wrong: Rows say "none left out", but the row's own link "Every record of this kind for Ireland, 2025, in Explore" shows 16 records, not 11. Five records about the country or about entries are neither added nor listed, though the page says it "lists every figure it left out, with the reason".
evidence: t1: 11 added, "none left out". The Explore link gives "16 of 4,349 figures". Records not listed: m-4bce825d59 and m-168167802b (all Irish data centres, CSO, 7,663 GWh), m-3f842bdd95 (Q4 2025 only), m-d348fa037b (an entry copy of Amazon Clonshaugh, 3,673,332 GJ), m-055775204e (an entry copy of Equinix DB5). t3: 6 added, the link shows 12. t5: 11 added, the link shows 22.
suggested_fix: List these under "Left out" with the reason (rule 1: about a country or an entry, not a site), or say "and N records about the country or entries, never added (rule 1)".

what_is_wrong: Some definitions show raw field names and nested brackets.
evidence: t19 and t22: "grid electricity, whole building as filed (type: Data Center (largestpropertyusetype=Data Center))". t23 and t25: "(type: Data Center (beudo_property_type=Manufacturing/Industrial))". The same text appears in the left-out lists of t18 to t28.
suggested_fix: Write them in plain words, e.g. "property type as filed: Data Center (Seattle's 'largest property use' field)" and "filed as a datacenter, Cambridge lists the property as manufacturing/industrial".

what_is_wrong: The filters and search are not kept in the address, so reloading or sharing the page loses them. Map and Explore keep theirs.
evidence: Chose Ireland and reloaded: the select was back to "Every country", "47 of 47 shown", and the address had no query.
suggested_fix: Write the country, topic and search into the address (replaceState) and read them on load.

location: search matching names inside closed lists
what_is_wrong: The search also matches site names inside closed lists, but those lists stay closed, so the reader cannot see why a row matched.
evidence: Search "Stella Towers" shows t20, t24 and t27 with their lists closed. The name is only visible after opening each list.
suggested_fix: Open the list of each row matched only inside its list, or mark the match ("matches a site in the list").

what_is_wrong: The two filter selects are labelled with their default option ("Every country", "Every topic"), so a screen reader announces "Every country, Ireland".
evidence: aria-label="Every country" and aria-label="Every topic" on the selects.
suggested_fix: Label them "Country" and "Topic".

what_is_wrong: Checked: dates are newest first, the count matches, and the feed agrees.
evidence: 20 November 2026 (10 entries), 17 November 2026 (18), 16 November 2026 · version 1.0.0 (10). 38 entries, matching the eyebrow's 38. No repeated ids. feed.xml has the same 38 entries in the same order. Note: this page, feed.xml, totals.html, index.html and brief.html were rewritten during the check (21:35 to 21:38 UTC); the final pass ran on the current files.

what_is_wrong: Checked: changes.html#<id> scrolls to that entry.
evidence: At 1280 and 390 px, #2026-11-20-totals-that-can-be-added, #2026-11-20-site-notes-in-full, #2026-11-17-a-check-of-the-graph and #d-2026-11-16 land with the entry at the top (top = 0). #2026-11-16-licence stops 410 px down because the page ends there. Clicking an entry's heading sets its anchor. Screenshot changes_phone_light_anchor_scotland.png.

what_is_wrong: Checked: the links work, and the page fits a phone in both schemes.
evidence: All 58 local links resolve, including index.html#global-datacentre-counts-directory-and-records, #uk-scotland-datacentre-directions-2026 and #us-nei-datacenter-facilities-2020-2023, which the index draws by script and which land at their entries. The 53 repository links are well formed (blob/main or tree/main paths). No overflow at 390 px in light or dark.

what_is_wrong: Within a day the entries are not newest first. The site counts in the entries show the order of events was 608, then 613, then 629 placed sites, but "Five more sites placed, a second pass" (613) is listed above "Coordinates from federal datasets" (629), which is above "198 US sites placed from their addresses" (608). The top entry, "UK sites on the map", says Digital Realty Redhill is not placed, while "Five more sites placed" below it places Redhill.
evidence: Entries 9 to 12 of 17 November end "613 of the 984 sites are now on the map", "629 of the 984 ...", "608 of the 984 ...". The feed gives every entry of a day the same time (T00:00:00Z).
suggested_fix: Order each day's entries by when they happened (newest first), or say that within a day they are grouped by subject. Give feed entries distinct times so readers keep the order.

what_is_wrong: "38 changes since the first shared version" includes the 10 entries of 16 November, which are the first shared version (1.0.0) itself.
evidence: The 16 November heading reads "16 November 2026 · version 1.0.0" and holds 10 of the 38 entries.
suggested_fix: Write "38 changes, from the first shared version (1.0.0) on", or count only the 28 that came after it.

what_is_wrong: An entry reached by its anchor is not highlighted. For entries near the end, which cannot be scrolled to the top, nothing shows which entry the link meant.
evidence: changes.html#2026-11-16-licence: the entry stops 410 px down; background transparent, no outline (no :target style).
suggested_fix: Add a :target style to .chg article, e.g. a paper-2 background or an accent left border.

file: docs/sites, org, country, doc pages; explore.html; totals.html
location: footer links "Report a problem with this page" and "Send a record the ledger does not have"
what_is_wrong: Checked: on six pages both footer links have well-formed addresses that fill the form's title and fields.
evidence: Pages: sites/irl-amazon-airton-road-tallaght-dub56-p1173.html, org/co-amazon.html, country/IRL.html, doc/d-ecd1820466.html, explore.html, totals.html. Every link goes to github.com/kn0wledgebfre3-sys/compute-ledger/issues/new with template=correction.yml or new-record.yml. The title is "Correction: <page name>" or "Record: <page name>". The fields filled, figure and subject, are ids in those forms. "figure" equals the page's own canonical address, and the subject is the page's name. rel=noopener. Every address decodes cleanly.

file: docs/sites, org, doc pages; totals.html -> explore.html
what_is_wrong: Checked: the link opens Explore with that one figure shown and its details open, including "Report an error in this figure".
evidence: The first link on the site page (m-887fca25bd), the organisation page (m-4084397436), the document page (m-033ab4030b) and a totals list's "the figure" each open explore.html#m-... with the banner "Showing one figure. Show every figure" and "1 of 4,349 figures". The details are open (aria-expanded true) with the citation, and the report link is issues/new?template=correction.yml&title=Correction: m-887fca25bd (Electricity used, Amazon Airton Road ...)&figure=m-887fca25bd. Closing and reopening works, and "Show every figure" returns to 4,349. A corrected id (m-1275fed334) leads to m-598aabc9e3 with a note, and an unknown id says "No figure has the id ...". All 8,677 figure links in the site point at existing ids. No overflow at 390 px.

location: single figure opened from a link
what_is_wrong: Explore opens at the top of the page. The one figure starts at the bottom of the first screen, and its open details, with the citation and the report link, start below it, so a reader may not see that the details are open.
evidence: At 1280 x 900 the details row spans y=970 to 1620 while the window is 900 tall, and the page is not scrolled. Screenshot explore_desktop_light_single_from_sites.png. The browser's own jump to #m-... happens before the row exists.
suggested_fix: After drawing a single figure, scroll its row into view (e.g. scrollIntoView on the row, block start).

location: figure on a country page without "Cite or report this figure"
what_is_wrong: Country pages have no "Cite or report this figure" link. country/IRL.html shows the directory's count of 135 datacentres, a ledger figure, with no link to cite or report it. The 20 November changelog says every figure on a country page links to its citation and correction form.
evidence: country/IRL.html: 0 links to explore.html#m-. The count 135 is figure m-73ed6c245c, and the United Kingdom's 608 is m-f2c29395a5. The document page doc/d-db758963c0.html does carry the links.
suggested_fix: Add "Cite or report this figure" after the directory count on every country page, or change the changelog's wording.

location: footer "Send a record the ledger does not have"
what_is_wrong: On pages that are not about one subject, the link fills the form's "Site, company or place" field with the page's name.
evidence: subject=Explore with title "Record: Explore". subject=the totals. subject=the map of sites. subject=what changed.
suggested_fix: On these pages leave the subject empty and use the title "Record: ".

location: footer "Report a problem with this page"
what_is_wrong: The link opens the figure-correction form, which requires "Link to the document" and "Page, table or section". Someone reporting a broken layout, link or label on a page has nothing to put in either field.
evidence: template=correction.yml. In .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/correction.yml, document and locator have validations: required: true.
suggested_fix: Add a short form for page problems (what is wrong, the page address) and link the footer to it, or make those two fields optional with a line saying they are for figure corrections.

what_is_wrong: Checked: the image is legible and accurate.
evidence: 1200 x 630. It reads "A public ledger · built from public records", "Compute Ledger", "The physical, social and economic footprint of AI compute, as the documents record it.", a Records box (regulators, courts, grid operators, statistics offices, registries), a Claims box (what companies and governments say, kept apart), the address kn0wledgebfre3-sys.github.io/compute-ledger and "Open data · CC BY 4.0". Everything is legible at full size and at a 500 px card (share_as_card_500px.png), and matches the site's own definitions, address and licence.

file: index.html, map.html, totals.html, a site page, an organisation page, a document page
what_is_wrong: Checked: each page carries the five preview tags, and a shared link would show something sensible.
evidence: Read in a browser from each page's head. og:title equals <title>. og:description is specific to the page (e.g. "Amazon.com, Inc.: what public records show about it and its sites, with its own statements kept apart."). og:image is the absolute address of assets/share.png, served as image/png and declared 1200x630, with og:image:alt. og:url equals the canonical address, which is the page's own address. twitter:card is summary_large_image. A scan of every page found all five tags on all 2,523 pages that are not redirects.

what_is_wrong: Five document pages have the same heading, og:title and og:description, so links to them look identical when shared. They are one dataset whose address differs only in the case of the host name, so one source is split across five pages.
evidence: Shared og:title: "NYC Building Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2023 to Present… · Compute Ledger". Their "Where to read it" addresses begin https://data., https://Data., https://dAta. and https://DATA.cityofnewyork.us. They hold 2, 62, 8, 126 and 2 figures.
suggested_fix: Lower-case the host name before grouping figures by document, so these become one page. Until then, add a distinguishing detail (date or figure count) to the title.

what_is_wrong: The headline has a thin grey hairline across the slot of each "e" in "Compute Ledger". A background rule at about y=517 runs into the sides of the Records and Claims boxes, between their two lines of text.
evidence: Enlarged crop share_zoom_title.png (hairlines in the three e's) and share_zoom_bottom.png. Pixels at y=175 inside the e's are grey (135,141,138) between paper-coloured pixels.
suggested_fix: Render the headline again without overlapping outlines (or with outlines merged), and stop the rules at the boxes or move them clear of the boxes.

what_is_wrong: The 16 pages left at retired site addresses redirect by meta refresh and carry no preview tags; their canonical is relative. An old link shared on social media would show no title, description or picture.
evidence: Example: sites/irl-google-dublin-grange-castle-data-center.html has no og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url or twitter:card, and canonical href="irl-google-grange-castle-ghg170.html".
suggested_fix: Copy the target page's preview tags into each redirect page and make the canonical absolute.

location: "Get the data" line: SQL link and its note
what_is_wrong: Checked: the new link and its note read well on desktop and phone.
evidence: At 1280 and 390 px, light and dark: "Query the tables with SQL in your browser" is followed by the bracketed note "(..., another site; it reads the CSV files and uploads nothing)". The line wraps without overflow. The note is 12.5px in the muted ink, about 6.8:1 in light and 8:1 in dark. The link is well formed: six CSV files from the repository (measurements, site_register, entries, entry_sources, entity_register, edges), all present in the repository, plus data/datasette-metadata.json, whose database name (data) and six table names match those files. Screenshots explore_desktop_light_getdata.png and explore_phone_dark_getdata.png.

location: "Get the data (version 1.0.0)" and the SQL link
what_is_wrong: The line is labelled version 1.0.0, but the SQL link reads the files on the main branch, which change after the release. A reader querying later gets newer data under a 1.0.0 label, and a citation of version 1.0.0 would not match.
evidence: Every csv= address is raw.githubusercontent.com/kn0wledgebfre3-sys/compute-ledger/main/data/...
suggested_fix: Point the CSV addresses at the release tag (e.g. .../v1.0.0/data/...) to match the label, or say in the note that it reads the latest files.

what_is_wrong: "Query the tables" loads six tables, while the item before it offers "every table". The note does not say how much the browser will download.
evidence: Six csv= files totalling about 4.8 MB (measurements.csv alone is 3.3 MB).
suggested_fix: Write e.g. "Query the six main tables with SQL in your browser (another site; it downloads about 5 MB of CSV from the repository into your browser and uploads nothing)".

location: "Get the data" line on a phone
what_is_wrong: On a phone, the middle-dot separators start lines ("· Every table as CSV") and link texts break across lines ("Query the tables with / SQL in your browser").
evidence: Screenshot explore_phone_dark_getdata.png.
suggested_fix: Join each separator to the item before it with a no-break space, or show the items as a short list on narrow screens.
